# Bonsai Backend

> Platform for building and operating governed, customer-facing conversational AI agents with structured stages, real-time voice/text sessions, and enterprise-grade operational controls.

Bonsai Backend is the runtime, API, and orchestration layer of the Bonsai platform. It handles conversation state, provider integrations, guardrails, audit, and real-time voice/text sessions. The companion UI is Bonsai Console (github.com/utter-one/bonsai-console).

Built with: Express 5, TypeScript, PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM, tsyringe IoC, Zod schemas as the OpenAPI source of truth.

## Project Model

Everything is scoped to a **Project**. A project is a self-contained conversational AI experience:

```
Project
├── Agents             ← persona, tone-of-voice, TTS settings
├── Stages             ← conversation phases (greeting, identify_issue, resolution, …)
│   └── Stage
│       ├── Prompt     ← Handlebars system prompt template
│       ├── Actions    ← triggers + effects (go_to_stage, run_script, call_webhook, …)
│       ├── Features   ← enabled capabilities for this stage
│       ├── Memory     ← stage-level memory settings
│       └── Lifecycle  ← enter/exit hooks, default classifier, knowledge tags
├── Classifiers        ← intent / routing / safety classification
├── Context Transformers ← LLM-powered parallel context extraction
├── Global Actions     ← actions available across all stages
├── Guardrails         ← project-wide safety / policy rules
├── Knowledge          ← FAQ categories + items injected per stage
├── Tools              ← callable capabilities exposed to the AI
├── Global Memory
│   ├── User Profile   ← persistent user profile schema
│   └── Constants      ← project-wide constants
├── Providers          ← LLM, TTS, ASR, Storage
├── Environments       ← named configs for environment promotion
├── API Keys           ← project-scoped keys for WebSocket/WebRTC clients
├── Conversations      ← live + historical sessions with events and artifacts
└── Users              ← end-user records with profile and session history
```

## How a Conversation Turn Works

```
User input (voice or text)
  → ASR transcription (if voice)
  → Content moderation
  → Classifiers + Guardrails + Context Transformers (parallel)
  → Action execution (effects, sequential):
      go_to_stage | run_script | call_webhook | call_tool
      modify_variables | modify_user_profile
      generate_response | end_conversation | abort_conversation
  → LLM response generation (streamed)
  → TTS synthesis (if voice output enabled, streamed)
  → Client receives text + audio chunks over WebSocket
```

## API Surfaces

### REST API — Administration

- **Base path:** `/api/`
- **Auth:** JWT bearer token (`POST /api/auth/login` → `POST /api/auth/refresh`)
- **First-run setup:** `POST /api/setup/initial-operator` (unauthenticated, only works before any operator exists)
- **OpenAPI spec:** `GET /openapi.json`
- **Swagger UI:** `GET /api-docs`

Key resource groups and their paths:

| Resource | Path prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Operators | `/api/operators` | User accounts for the admin panel |
| Projects | `/api/projects` | Top-level container for an AI experience |
| Agents | `/api/projects/:projectId/agents` | Persona + TTS config |
| Stages | `/api/projects/:projectId/stages` | Conversation phases |
| Classifiers | `/api/projects/:projectId/classifiers` | Intent / routing classifiers |
| Context Transformers | `/api/projects/:projectId/context-transformers` | Structured context extraction |
| Global Actions | `/api/projects/:projectId/global-actions` | Cross-stage behaviors |
| Guardrails | `/api/projects/:projectId/guardrails` | Policy enforcement |
| Knowledge | `/api/projects/:projectId/knowledge` | FAQ categories + items |
| Tools | `/api/projects/:projectId/tools` | Callable capabilities |
| Conversations | `/api/projects/:projectId/conversations` | Session history + events |
| Users | `/api/projects/:projectId/users` | End-user records |
| API Keys | `/api/projects/:projectId/api-keys` | Keys for WS/WebRTC clients |
| Providers | `/api/providers` | LLM / TTS / ASR / Storage configs |
| Environments | `/api/environments` | Config snapshots for promotion |
| Audit Logs | `/api/audit` | Immutable before/after snapshots |
| Analytics | `/api/analytics` | Latency + usage metrics |
| Secrets | `/api/secrets` | Encrypted secret storage |
| Scenarios / Testers | `/api/scenarios`, `/api/testers` | Automated conversation testing |

### WebSocket API — Live Sessions

**Endpoint:** `ws://<host>/ws`

All messages are JSON. Clients must authenticate before starting conversations.

#### Authentication handshake

Client → Server:
```json
{
  "requestId": "req-1",
  "type": "auth",
  "apiKey": "<project-api-key>",
  "sessionSettings": {
    "sendVoiceInput": true,
    "sendTextInput": true,
    "receiveVoiceOutput": true,
    "receiveTranscriptionUpdates": true,
    "receiveEvents": false,
    "sendAudioFormat": "pcm_16000",
    "receiveAudioFormat": "pcm_16000"
  }
}
```

Server → Client:
```json
{
  "type": "auth",
  "sessionId": "session_XXXXXXXXX",
  "projectSettings": { "projectId": "...", "acceptVoice": true, "generateVoice": true }
}
```

#### Message types (client → server)

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `auth` | Authenticate with API key |
| `start_conversation` | Begin a new conversation |
| `resume_conversation` | Resume an existing conversation |
| `end_conversation` | End the active conversation |
| `start_user_voice_input` | Signal start of voice input |
| `send_user_voice_chunk` | Stream base64-encoded audio chunk |
| `end_user_voice_input` | Signal end of voice input, trigger processing |
| `send_user_text_input` | Send a text message |
| `go_to_stage` | Navigate to a specific stage |
| `set_var` / `get_var` / `get_all_vars` | Manage conversation variables |
| `run_action` | Trigger a named action |
| `call_tool` | Invoke a registered tool |

#### Message types (server → client)

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `start_ai_generation_output` | AI is beginning to respond |
| `send_ai_voice_chunk` | Streamed base64 TTS audio chunk |
| `end_ai_generation_output` | AI response complete |
| `ai_transcribed_chunk` | Incremental AI text transcription |
| `user_transcribed_chunk` | Incremental ASR transcription of user voice |
| `conversation_event` | Structured event from the conversation pipeline |
| `conversation_event_update` | Update to an existing event |

Full JSON Schema for all WebSocket messages: `GET /websocket-contracts.json`

### WebRTC API — Low-Latency Voice

**Signaling endpoint:** `POST /api/webrtc/offer`

Same conversation protocol as WebSocket. Binary audio over an unordered DataChannel (`audio`), control messages over an ordered DataChannel (`control`). Auth via the `auth` JSON message over the `control` channel.

## Currently Supported Providers

| Type | Providers |
|---|---|
| LLM | OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Perplexity, Cohere, xAI |
| TTS | ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Azure, Deepgram, Cartesia, Amazon Polly |
| ASR | Azure, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Speechmatics |
| Storage | (configurable via provider system) |

## Backend Codebase Conventions

### Directory Structure

```
src/
  http/
    controllers/     ← ~30 Express controllers, one per domain
    contracts/       ← Zod schemas for request/response validation + OpenAPI
    middleware/      ← auth, requestContext, errorHandler, rateLimiter
  services/          ← Business logic (one service per domain)
  channels/
    websocket/       ← WebSocket channel host + contracts
    webrtc/          ← WebRTC channel host
    twilio-voice/    ← Twilio Voice channel
    twilio-messaging/← Twilio SMS channel
    whatsapp/        ← WhatsApp channel
    telegram/        ← Telegram channel
    handlers/        ← Message handlers (auto-registered via @ChannelMessageHandler)
  db/
    schema.ts        ← Drizzle ORM schema — single source of truth for DB
  scripts/           ← Build utilities (generateWebSocketSchemas.ts)
  errors.ts          ← Custom error classes (map to HTTP status codes)
  permissions.ts     ← RBAC permission strings (60+)
  server.ts          ← Express app factory + all route registration
  index.ts           ← Entry point

drizzle/             ← Generated SQL migration files (version controlled)
schemas/             ← Generated websocket-contracts.json
```

### Controller Pattern

```typescript
@singleton()
export class ExampleController {
  constructor(@inject(ExampleService) private readonly service: ExampleService) {}

  static getOpenAPIPaths(): RouteConfig[] { /* OpenAPI docs */ }

  registerRoutes(router: Router): void {
    router.post('/api/examples', asyncHandler(this.create.bind(this)));
  }

  private async create(req: Request, res: Response): Promise<void> {
    checkPermissions(req, [PERMISSIONS.EXAMPLE_WRITE]);
    const body = createExampleSchema.parse(req.body);
    const result = await this.service.create(body, req.context);
    res.status(201).json(result);
  }
}
```

- `@singleton()` on controllers, `@injectable()` on services
- Wrap all handlers with `asyncHandler()`
- Validate via `schema.parse(req.body / req.params / req.query)`
- `checkPermissions(req, [...])` at the start of every handler
- Services also call `this.requirePermission(context, PERMISSIONS.XXX)` for defense in depth

### Database Changes

1. Edit `src/db/schema.ts`
2. Update corresponding `src/http/contracts/` Zod schemas
3. Update services that reference changed columns
4. `npm run db:generate` → review `/drizzle/XXXX_*.sql`
5. `npm run db:migrate`
6. `npm run build`

### WebSocket Contract Changes

1. Edit files in `src/channels/websocket/contracts/`
2. Update `src/scripts/generateWebSocketSchemas.ts` if adding new top-level message types
3. Run `npm run schemas:generate` (also runs automatically on `npm run build`)

## Key Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # schemas:generate + db:migrate + tsx watch
npm run build        # schemas:generate + tsc → dist/
npm start            # db:migrate + node dist/
npm run db:generate  # Generate Drizzle migration from schema diff
npm run db:migrate   # Apply pending migrations
npm run db:studio    # Open Drizzle Studio
npm run schemas:generate  # Regenerate schemas/websocket-contracts.json
```

## Environment Variables

Required:
- `DB_CONNECTION_STRING` — PostgreSQL connection string
- `JWT_SECRET` — Min 32 characters, used to sign operator tokens

Important optional:
- `MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — Enables automatic migration of plain-text secrets in provider configs
- `CORS_ORIGIN` — Allowed CORS origin (default: `*`)
- `LOG_LEVEL` — pino log level (default: `info`)
- `TRUST_PROXY` — Set to `false` to disable (default: enabled)
- `WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` — WebSocket max payload (default: 10MB)
- `RATE_LIMIT_API_WINDOW_MS` / `RATE_LIMIT_API_MAX` — General API rate limiting
- `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_WINDOW_MS` / `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX` — Auth endpoint rate limiting

## Quick Start (Docker Compose)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/utter-one/bonsai.git
cd bonsai/compose
cp env.example .env
# Set JWT_SECRET to a random value of at least 32 characters
docker compose up -d
```

- Backend API: `http://localhost:3000`
- Swagger UI: `http://localhost:3000/api-docs`
- OpenAPI spec: `http://localhost:3000/openapi.json`
- WebSocket contracts: `http://localhost:3000/websocket-contracts.json`
- LLM guide: `http://localhost:3000/llms.txt`

- [Source repository](https://github.com/utter-one/bonsai): Full source code with Dockerfile and compose stack
- [Bonsai Console](https://github.com/utter-one/bonsai-console): Companion visual admin panel

- [WebSocket contracts](./websocket-contracts.json): JSON Schema for all real-time message types (relative to running instance)
